newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican sugar union calls off strike for pay hike.
newsitem.headline: Mexican sugar union calls off strike for pay hike.

text.p: Mexico's 62,000 unionized sugar mill workers have called off a strike in return for a 26 percent pay increase, national TV network Televisa said Monday.

The workers, who belong to the National Sugar Workers' Union, had refused to man mills for the 1996-1997 harvest which was scheduled to start Nov 15, originally demanding a 56 percent increase in salaries.
Radio network Radio red confirmed the accord of a 26 percent increase, plus unspecified benefits.
Union workers, who operate the country's 61 active mills, had been on strike for two days in a traditional tussle at start of the sugar harvest tussle with mill owners.

Few mills operate early in the November-June cycle, although the National Sugar Chamber had programmed one mill at Atencingo in the state of Mexico to crank up machinery in mid-November with others coming on line before the month end. Peak mill production is in January and February.
Spokesmen for the union and the sugar chamber, which represents the mills, were not immediately available to confirm the reports.
